reading.body:
QTS Sacramento publishes 4 MW of critical power capacity, which at AI training densities of 40 kW per rack represents roughly 100 racks, or at colocation densities of 10 kW per rack, roughly 400 racks.

The facility occupies a 7-acre site with a dedicated on-site substation, water-side economizers, and well water cooling. It holds Energy Star certification. Among five California facilities with published capacity figures, it ranks fourth at 2.4 percent of the 170 MW total those five report. California has 103 mapped data center facilities, but 98 of them publish no megawatt figure, so actual state capacity is substantially larger than published figures reveal.

At this scale, the campus supports a real but limited AI workload. One hundred racks cannot run a large-scale training cluster. The operator's published specifications do not disclose tenant mix or use cases, so whether this facility serves inference, enterprise AI, or mixed colocation demand is unknown. The power constraint is visible—4 MW is the binding input—but whether that power can expand is not addressed in operator disclosures.
